newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum premiums softer, alloy/scrap firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum premiums softer, alloy/scrap firmer.

text.p: U.S. aluminum premiums have softened a touch, but there was no panic dumping by physical merchants yet as the contango on LME shrivelled up Thursday.
Premiums have eased back a touch to 5.00 to 5.50 cents a lb over LME cash in the Midwest, down 0.25 cent over the past week.
As the LME contango disappears, physical merchants lose the financing for their stocks and may be tempted to dump some metal, traders said.
"We are not seeing any metal being dumped -- we only saw the LME contango disappearing today. It will take a while to see what happens," a dealer said.
Another physical merchant said that release orders for metal in the Midwest were next due on Feb 15, when any metal would be dumped by merchants if a solid backwardation is established.
Meanwhile, aluminum alloy prices in the Midwest continued with their steady climb and were up to 74 to 75 cents a lb for benchmark A380 alloy.
"Some people think the LME alloy contract is also going into backwardation because there is very good demand for prompt metal in Europe," a West Coast smelter official said.
There was also talk of alloy from the U.S. moving to Europe.
The hike in alloy prices were badly needed by smelters after scrap prices rose a few weeks ago.

However, smelter officials said scrap was still in relatively tight supply and prices have surged a few cents again in the past week, leaving smelter margins once more under pressure and looking for further hikes in alloy prices.
